clue.text: Model sermon could be a fearsome thing

indicators.note: saying the letters could be something else invites rearranging them into another word

blocks.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car
taken as written

explanation.surface: A preacher's exemplary address turns out to be something terrifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as an adjective praising the sermon, but it is the Model T, giving one letter to add to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster is a frightening creature or object, so it fits a fearsome thing exactly.

clue.text: Beaks begin as conveyers of offerings

indicators.note: begin keeps only the start of the word, dropping its ending

blocks.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge

explanation.surface: Birds' bills start off carrying gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first four letters of the word for beaks are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi were the wise men who brought gold, frankincense and myrrh as gifts to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Components Simon mislaid, lacking responsibility

indicators.note: mislaid suggests things laid out wrongly, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Simon carelessly lost some parts, showing he is not reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: Non compos mentis is Latin for not of sound mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not of sound mind cannot be held legally accountable, lacking capacity for their actions.

clue.text: Die in attempt to get with it

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
to die is to end

explanation.surface: Someone risks death in an effort to stay fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: With it is slang for fashionable and up to date, the same sense as trendy.

clue.text: Girl turns up in right place for vacation

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading the word from bottom to top
in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: Rose is a girl's name
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A young woman appears at just the right holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a holiday destination, a place people go to on vacation.

clue.text: Firm's custom is to have a single partner

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a habit is a custom or regular practice

explanation.surface: A company's policy sounds like a rule on monogamy for its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stretches a little: to cohabit is to live with one partner without marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who cohabit live together as a pair, sharing a home with one chosen companion.

clue.text: Ravel (sic) designed instruments

indicators.note: designed means freshly arranged, so the letters are set in a new pattern

blocks.note: the composer's name plus the bracketed word

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel, spelt correctly, designed some musical instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: '(sic)' looks like an editor's note but is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavier is a keyboard instrument, such as a harpsichord or clavichord.

clue.text: Hard boundary, hard to go over - it's prickly

indicators.note: over means the word before it is turned back to front

blocks.note: H is the pencil grading for hard
an edge is a boundary
H for hard again
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tough barrier that is hard to climb is a spiky one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgehog is a small mammal covered in sharp spines, so it is a prickly creature.

clue.text: Hear about fiddle playing for a funeral

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and moved around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mourner learns of a violinist performing at a funeral service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle playing' looks like violin music; 'playing' is the anagram signal and fiddle is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burial of the Dead is the Prayer Book's service for interring a body, the liturgy used at a funeral.

clue.text: Erstwhile bit of an opera

blocks.note: first meaning: an old British coin worth three pence, withdrawn in 1971
second meaning: the word in Brecht and Weill's musical play title

explanation.walkthrough: The threepenny bit was a small pre-decimal British coin; The Threepenny Opera is Brecht and Weill's 1928 work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes both the old coin's name, a threepenny bit, and the title The Threepenny Opera.

clue.text: Type we need information about

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone asks for details on what sort of thing is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind, especially of art or writing, so it is a sort or class.

clue.text: One's words may lead to action

definitions.text: One's words may lead to action

blocks.clueFragment: One's words may lead to action
blocks.note: surface reading: an inspiring speaker whose talk spurs people to do things
setter's reading: legal action, a lawsuit brought over spoken defamation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' sounds like getting things done, but here it is a court action, the result of damaging false speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who utters false damaging statements about another may well be sued for it in court.

clue.text: Queue at frontier - luggage may be near the limit

blocks.note: a line of people waiting at a border
a case is a suitcase

explanation.surface: Travellers wait at customs, a bag perhaps just over the weight allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near the limit' reads as the weight allowance in the surface; it is the definition of an expression for a doubtful case.
explanation.definitionFit: A borderline case is one that sits right at the threshold, hard to classify either way.

clue.text: Time, perhaps, for police raid

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A set hour is planned for a police swoop.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate anagram signal; the setter leaves the solver to rearrange the letters of the two words. Time is the American news magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is a weekly news magazine, an example of a publication issued at regular intervals.

clue.text: Demonstration by  Consignia? ...

blocks.note: Consignia was the short-lived name of the former British Post Office

explanation.surface: A display put on by the renamed postal company, with a trail into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2001 the Post Office renamed itself Consignia, making Consignia an EX-PO, former Post Office. The dots link to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exhibition or show, where products or ideas are put on public display.

clue.text: ... Tarry - stuff could be in the post

definitions.text: Tarry - stuff could be in the post

blocks.clueFragment: Tarry - stuff could be in the post
blocks.note: surface reading: following on from the mail clue, wait, something may be in the mail
setter's reading: a tar-like substance that soaks into a wooden fence post

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tarry' looks like a verb meaning wait, and 'post' seems to continue the Post Office theme; really it is a tar-based wood preservative painted on posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is an oily tar distillate used to preserve timber such as fence posts.

clue.text: One discontented king outdoing Uriah?

blocks.note: GR, Georgius Rex, King George
Dickens's Uriah Heep is forever 'umble, so outdoing him is being 'umbler

explanation.surface: A dissatisfied monarch tries to outdo a Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep in David Copperfield constantly calls himself 'umble, dropping the H; going one better is 'umbler.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumbler complains constantly, someone who is unhappy and lets everyone know it.

clue.text: Time for parental  preparation?

indicators.note: preparation means making ready, so the letters are prepared afresh in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Expectant mothers and fathers get ready for the baby's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the months before birth are when parents get ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Prenatal means before birth, the period when expectant parents prepare for the baby.

clue.text: They may have you covered, but certainly won't initiate fire

blocks.note: surface reading: people protecting you, like a gunman or bodyguard
setter's reading: companies providing policies would never want to start a blaze they must pay out on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered' and 'fire' suggest gunmen; the cover is a policy, and fire is the hazard insured against.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance companies give cover, paying out for losses such as fire damage to a policyholder.

clue.text: School education first to be given weight

indicators.note: first asks for only the leading letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the opening letter of education
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A school puts academic learning above everything and treats it seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a well-known English public school, so it is a specific example of a school.

clue.text: I forgot to say, youth club leaders may explode, so mind!

indicators.note: leaders asks for the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: a postscript, added when the writer forgot something
the opening letters of the two words
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: A worried afterthought: the youth club's organisers might lose their temper, so watch out!
explanation.definitionFit: Psyche is the human soul or mind, from the Greek word for breath or spirit.

clue.text: A flyer cut short by drink

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a bittern is a marsh bird

explanation.surface: A pilot's trip was curtailed because of alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a well-hopped English ale, a common pub drink.

clue.text: With abstruse reading, impress the highest in Oxford

indicators.note: abstruse means obscure and hard to follow, so the letters are jumbled out of plain sense

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clever, obscure study impresses the top scholars at Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The highest in Oxford' suggests top dons; it is the city's tallest buildings, its famous spires.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford is nicknamed the city of dreaming spires after Matthew Arnold's poem; spires are its tallest structures.

clue.text: Half the alphabet is minute

blocks.note: the first thirteen letters run from A to M

explanation.surface: Covering just the first part of the ABC takes no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like a unit of time; read it as tiny. The first half of the alphabet runs A to M.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is a tiny particle, so it stands for something minute in size.

clue.text: Constant withdrawal from capital turning City into stimulating reaction

indicators.note: withdrawal means something is taken out of the word that follows
turning means the word after it is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: pi is the mathematical constant
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Steady flight of money from a capital transforms a city's economy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PI out of CAPITAL to leave CATAL, then add CITY backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction, so catalytic describes something that stimulates one.

clue.text: Paper peculatio

blocks.note: the Financial Times, known by its initials with the article in front

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about embezzlement, in two terse words.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, a British business newspaper. Peculatio is Latin for embezzlement of public money.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculation is embezzling funds held in trust, a form of stealing what belongs to others.

clue.text: A sin soldiers left behind as part of cleansing

indicators.note: behind tells us that the final piece comes after the others

blocks.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins
RA is the Royal Artillery
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A wrong committed by troops is left behind them in a purification ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustral means relating to ritual purification, as in lustral water used in ceremonies of washing.

clue.text: Confused model with  a right to a peerage

indicators.note: something confused is mixed up, so its letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bewildered fashion model is somehow entitled to a seat in the Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank or title of an earl, one of the grades of the British nobility.
